tweets: An external contract can seize control flow and call back before your function finishes.
This allows a malicious caller to re-enter your code mid-execution.
The root cause is updating state after the external call, relying on stale data.
Remediation requires performing all internal state changes before any external interaction.
This approach is known as the Checks-Effects-Interactions pattern.
A reentrancy lock blocks unwanted callbacks into protected paths but does not stop control passing to external callees.
